products.name: Intune Enrollment-Time Device Grouping — Prerequisites, Setup & Troubleshooting (Autopilot Device Preparation + Apple ADE) — Commercial
products.short_description: The definitive fix for Intune Enrollment-Time Grouping failures — the Intune Provisioning Client must own an Assigned, cloud-only Security group, plus the full prerequisite matrix, RBAC-scope rules, and a symptom→root-cause tree (incl. the Azure-log red herring) — for Windows Autopilot device preparation AND Apple ADE. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
products.description:
Fix the "Intune Provisioning Client is not an owner" enrollment-grouping failure — for Autopilot and Apple ADE

You configure a device group on a Windows Autopilot device-preparation policy or an Apple ADE enrollment policy, it saves… and fails: "Unable to save device group … the Intune Provisioning Client application is not an owner." The group looks right, the policy is valid, yet Enrollment-Time Grouping won't commit — and the portal buries you in unrelated AuthorizationFailed Azure-log errors that send you chasing the wrong thing. This solution is the definitive prerequisites, setup, and diagnostic playbook: the exact group configuration, the required Intune Provisioning Client owner, the RBAC scope rules, and a symptom→root-cause tree that maps each error string to its real cause — so enrollment-time grouping saves and populates devices, on Windows and Apple.

Run it yourself — simpler, cheaper, and proven

You do not need a consultant. The package hands you the field-tested method as self-guided, click-by-click documentation a competent admin can follow end to end — backed by ready-to-run PowerShell.

  • Simpler — exact, ordered steps with full navigation paths; every object you create is named and reused through testing and troubleshooting.
  • Cheaper — one fixed price instead of an open meter; a comparable consulting engagement runs well into the thousands per day. Reusable on every rollout.
  • Tested — a pilot-first method (Assess → Configure → Pilot → Validate → Expand) with explicit pass/fail gates.

What's inside

  • Solution Overview — what Enrollment-Time Grouping is and the mechanism that trips everyone up: the Intune Provisioning Client service principal must own the assigned group so Intune can add devices at enrollment. Applies to Windows Autopilot device preparation AND Apple ADE (shared / no user affinity) — Microsoft documents it for Windows; Apple uses the same backend with little Apple-specific documentation.
  • Prerequisites Matrix — every requirement with how to verify/implement: Security group, Assigned membership (never Dynamic), Cloud-only (not synced from on-prem AD), not mail-enabled, not Entra-role-assignable, ideally empty, the Intune Provisioning Client as Owner (AppId f1346770-5b25-470b-88bd-d5744ab7952c), the admin able to manage the group, and the group inside the admin's Intune RBAC scope groups.
  • Setup Guide (both platforms) — create the group to spec, add the Intune Provisioning Client owner (match by AppId; provision the SP if absent), then wire it to a Windows Autopilot device-preparation policy and an Apple ADE enrollment-token policy — named steps, propagation waits, and validation.
  • Diagnostic Playbook — a symptom→root-cause decision tree: the generic "Updating device group for Apple enrollment policy" hang, the definitive "…Intune Provisioning Client application is not an owner" error, the Azure Activity Log AuthorizationFailed / microsoft.insights/eventtypes/values/read red herring (ignore it), propagation delay, SP-named-differently, SP-missing, RBAC-scope, and how to inspect the real backend error via Graph / browser dev tools before escalating to Microsoft.
  • 5 PowerShell (Graph) tools — group-readiness assessment (type/membership/source/mail/role-assignable/owner), an add-owner remediation (-WhatIf), a full prereq + RBAC-scope validator, a diagnostic report that maps the observed error to its cause, and a scope/config helper — read-only or dry-run by default, no secrets in code.

The repeatable way

Every solution follows the same repeatable shape, so each deployment feels familiar and low-risk — buy once, reuse the playbook for the next wave and the next project.

The bottom line

Enrollment-Time Grouping that saves and populates devices at enrollment — the Provisioning Client owning the right group, prerequisites met, and every error string mapped to its real cause — so Autopilot and Apple ADE deployments stop failing on Save.

What you receive — every file in your download

This package is delivered as downloadable files you keep and reuse across unlimited devices — nothing is left out and nothing else is required:

  • Implementation Guide (PDF) — the complete, click-by-click solution: solution overview, requirements, step-by-step implementation, testing & validation, troubleshooting, best practices.
  • PowerShell Scripts (ZIP) — 5 ready-to-run scripts (read-only discovery/validation/reporting; remediation defaults to a safe preview):
    • ETDG-Assess-GroupReadiness.ps1 — report whether a target group meets the Enrollment-Time Grouping spec and is owned by the Intune Provisioning Client (read-only)
    • ETDG-Config.ps1 — shared configuration + Graph connection helper for the Enrollment-Time Device Grouping toolkit (read-only)
    • ETDG-Get-DiagnosticReport.ps1 — map an observed Enrollment-Time Grouping error/state to its likely root cause, and flag the Azure Activity Log red herring (read-only)
    • ETDG-Set-ProvisioningClientOwner.ps1 — add the Intune Provisioning Client service principal as an Owner of the target group (preview-first, -WhatIf default)
    • ETDG-Test-EnrollmentGroupPrereqs.ps1 — full prerequisite validation: group spec (R1-R7), Provisioning Client SP exists, and the admin's Intune RBAC scope groups (R9). Read-only

Delivered as a Word document and PDF, plus all PowerShell scripts in a single ZIP — yours to keep and reuse.
